program_meta.program_name: Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), EECS Department, College of Engineering (administered through the Rackham Graduate School). Note: several of the strongest matches below sit in the ECE Division of EECS, which runs a SEPARATE PhD admission (ECE PhD) — Liyue Shen, Qing Qu, Clayton Scott, Samet Oymak and Jeffrey Fessler are ECE, not CSE.
program_meta.sop_limit: 3 pages. CSE 'How to Apply' page, verbatim: 'Your statement of purpose should be a concise, well-written document about your academic and/or research background, as well as your career goals. Additionally, it should communicate how CSE's graduate program will help you meet your career and educational objectives. The statement of purpose has a 3 page limit.' Rackham adds formatting rules: margins at least one inch, and a header on each document giving document type ('Academic Statement of Purpose'), your name, the program name, and your 8-digit U-M ID if known. Rackham itself does not set a length ('Questions about length should be directed to the program') — so the operative cap is CSE's 3 pages. CONFIRMED: the 3-page cap the task expected is real.
program_meta.extra_essays: SEPARATE Personal Statement, 500 words. CSE verbatim: 'The personal statement has a 500 word limit and is [not] identical to the statement of purpose.' Rackham verbatim: 'The personal statement has a 500 word limit and should be different from your Academic Statement of Purpose.' Rackham prompt: 'How have your background and life experiences, including cultural, geographical, financial, educational, or other opportunities or challenges, motivated your decision to pursue a graduate degree at the University of Michigan?' CONFIRMED: separate ~500-word Personal Statement is real and mandatory. Also required: CV or resume (third mandatory upload). Also on the application: 'Select up to five CSE faculty whose research interests align with yours and whom you would consider as potential research advisors.' CSE further states: 'if you do not see a specific faculty member listed in the application dropdown, please include their name in another area of the application (e.g. the statement of purpose or the Additional Information section). The application can be searched by faculty using keywords.'
program_meta.deadline_fall_2027: December 15, 11:59 PM ET for the PhD (CSE table: 'PhD Application Deadline — December 15th, 11:59 PM ET'; 'For full admission and financial aid consideration, applications to the doctoral program must be completed and submitted by December 15th.'). For Fall 2027 entry that is December 15, 2026. Master's deadline is January 15, 11:59 PM ET. Supporting materials (letters, transcripts, test scores) should arrive by the deadline. CSE notes the FA2027 fee-waiver process is not yet posted: 'Please check back again in the fall for any updates regarding fee waivers for the FA 2027 application cycle.'
program_meta.lor_count: 3. CSE verbatim: 'Request 3 letters of recommendation from people who are familiar with your academic performance and research potential.' Must be submitted through the online system — 'we do not accept letters by email, physical mail, or other systems (e.g. Interfolio)'. Applicants must select 'Yes' to 'Use Online Recommendation System', and recommenders must be registered BEFORE the application is submitted. CSE also notes successful applicants 'usually have an undergraduate GPA of at least 3.5/4.0 (although this is not a hard requirement) and three strong letters of recommendation.'
program_meta.gre: Not considered. CSE verbatim heading: 'GRE scores are not considered in the admissions review of PhD or Master's applications.' Rackham verbatim: 'GRE general test scores are no longer included in the admissions process for Rackham's doctoral programs.' CONFIRMED — do not send scores.
program_meta.english_test: Required unless exempt. There is NO blanket India exemption. Rackham exemption criteria (verbatim list) include: 'You completed all of your undergraduate education and earned an undergraduate degree at an institution where the language of instruction is English only.' Manipal Institute of Technology Bengaluru teaches in English, so Akshat most likely qualifies — but Rackham requires proof: 'Applicants are required to upload the front and back of their transcript. Most universities indicate the language of the institution on the back of the transcript. If it is not indicated on the transcript, applicants can submit a letter from the Registrar's Office, or equivalent, on university letterhead confirming the language of instruction.' Applicants self-assess at application time and are re-checked if recommended for admission. Rackham minimums if a test IS needed: TOEFL iBT (incl. ITP Plus and Special Home Edition) — 'Before January 21, 2026 = 84. January 21, 2026 and after = 4.5' [reported verbatim; the second figure reflects the new TOEFL scale]; TOEFL iBT Paper Test — no overall score, minimum sections Reading 23 / Listening 23 / Writing 21; IELTS Academic 6.5 (one-skill retake accepted); MET 4-skill overall 59; ECPE Certificate of Proficiency. Scores valid 2 years; institution code 1839; photocopies/faxes not accepted. Some programs require higher scores than Rackham — CSE does not publish a higher bar on its How to Apply page.
program_meta.app_fee: $90 for non-U.S. citizens (Rackham: 'United States citizens and those with permanent resident visa status: $75 / Non-U.S. citizens: $90 / Current Rackham student: $10'). Rackham's own fee-waiver program is limited to U.S. citizens and permanent residents with demonstrated financial need, so it does NOT apply to Akshat. CSE runs a separate PhD-applicant fee waiver; as of 2026-08-28 the page reads 'Fee waiver application for FA 2026 is closed and is no longer accepting applications' with FA2027 details to be posted in the fall — worth re-checking in October 2026.

program_meta.advisor_model: Department admission with strong advisor signalling — NOT a hard advisor-first model and NOT rotations. The application asks you to 'Select up to five CSE faculty whose research interests align with yours and whom you would consider as potential research advisors', and CSE explicitly says faculty search applications by keyword, so naming professors in the SOP/Additional Information matters. Funding is guaranteed by the department: 'We guarantee PhD students full funding as long as they are making satisfactory progress towards the degree.' Several individual faculty (Dereziński, Makar, Shen, Park, Yu) independently instruct applicants to apply to the program and list/mention their name rather than seek pre-admission commitments.
program_meta.ms_research_access: MS admission carries no funding: 'Admission to the M.S. program is not accompanied by funding, but there are opportunities for financial support after beginning the program.' Research access for master's students is real but limited and faculty-dependent — e.g. Maggie Makar states verbatim 'I am not involved in the masters program at all', while Liyue Shen and Clayton Scott do take master's students into projects. There is a CSE dual-degree / add-a-degree route requiring a Statement of Purpose, Personal Statement and '1 Letter of Recommendation from a CSE faculty member'. Master's deadline is January 15. Note: 'If you have a MS or PhD in computer science or an equivalent field from another institution, you cannot apply for the same degree at the University of Michigan.'
program_meta.notes: A master's degree is NOT required to apply to the PhD: 'We expect applicants to both the Master's and PhD programs to have earned their bachelor's degrees by the time they matriculate... A master's degree is not required to apply to the PhD program.' cse.engin.umich.edu and ece.engin.umich.edu sit behind Cloudflare bot protection and return 403 to plain fetchers; all CSE figures here were read from the live rendered pages in a browser session on 2026-08-28. STRATEGIC NOTE FOR AKSHAT: Michigan's best matches for his exact profile (diffusion-as-pretraining for medical imaging, hierarchy-consistent structured prediction, label-efficient learning) are split across TWO admissions pipelines — Stella Yu and Jeong Joon Park are reachable through the CSE PhD, while Liyue Shen and Qing Qu require the ECE PhD. Liyue Shen's recruiting page notes PhD students 'can be co-advised with other senior faculty members in the SIP&ML area at Umich ECE'. If CSE is the fixed target, Yu + Park are the SOP anchors; if the Shen/Qu pairing is the real draw, an ECE application is the correct vehicle and should be considered as a second Michigan application.

faculty.department: EECS — ECE Division (Electrical and Computer Engineering); affiliated with MIDAS, MICDE, MMRI
faculty.research_areas: Biomedical AI; medical image analysis; diffusion / score-based generative models; implicit neural representation learning; multimodal medical foundation models; data-efficient learning (self-/un-/semi-supervised) with limited labels; robust learning with missing data and noisy labels; inverse problems in imaging
faculty.why_match: Her ICML'26 paper 'Evaluating the Representation Space of Diffusion Models via Self-Supervised Principles' asks exactly the question Akshat's DDPM work left open: what does a diffusion model's internal representation actually encode, and when is it useful downstream. Akshat pretrained a DDPM on unlabelled abdominal CT and transferred the encoder to organ segmentation — liver Dice rose 0.751 to 0.928 and a FROZEN encoder retained 87% of the fine-tuned liver Dice, but the same frozen encoder FAILED on kidney, falling below random initialisation. That per-structure asymmetry is a representation-space question, not a segmentation question, and her self-supervised probing framework plus 'Weak Diffusion Priors Can Still Achieve Strong Inverse-Problem Performance' (ICML'26 Spotlight) — which shows a deliberately weakened prior still carries usable structure — is the sharpest available instrument for testing it. Her stated recruiting directions literally include 'Data-efficient learning such as self- / un- / semi-supervised learning with limited data / labels', which is Akshat's spine-MRI pseudo-labelling result (54 labelled images, teacher 0.735 mIoU to student 0.816 mIoU).

faculty.department: EECS — Computer Science and Engineering; Adjunct Professor of Robotics; Michigan AI Lab core faculty
faculty.lab: Stella Yu's vision group (Michigan AI Lab)
faculty.research_areas: Computer vision, human vision, machine learning, robotics; hierarchical / structure-aware recognition; unsupervised and minimally-supervised segmentation and representation learning; structural inductive biases (symmetry, part-whole hierarchies, geometric constraints); applications to science and medicine
faculty.why_match: She is the one person at Michigan working directly on Akshat's HiME problem. Her 'Visually Consistent Hierarchical Recognition' (HCAST, ICLR 2025) and 'Free-Grained Hierarchical Recognition' (CVPR 2026) attack taxonomy-consistent prediction as a representation and decoding problem rather than a post-hoc repair problem — which is exactly HiME's claim: per-level conditional sigmoids composed by the chain rule mean a child's probability cannot exceed its parent's, so the prediction set is upward-closed and hierarchy consistency holds BY CONSTRUCTION (Prop. 1), verified at 1.000 across five backbones on Galaxy Zoo 2 (239,573 images, 37 classes, 4 levels, 95.8% decision-level accuracy) with ~0.01% parameter overhead. Critically, Akshat's own Table V contains the awkward finding her line of work is built to explain: the structural constraint COSTS accuracy under a frozen ViT-B/16 encoder (0.858 vs 0.888 flat) and is free under full fine-tuning (0.952). Her third research theme is stated verbatim as 'Efficient Structure-Aware Machine Learning Models... My work incorporates structural inductive biases such as symmetry, part-whole hierarchies, and geometric constraints'. Her 'Unsupervised Hierarchical Semantic Segmentation' and 'Learning Visual Groupings and Representations with Minimal Human Labels' (Tsung-Wei Ke thesis) also line up with Akshat's label-efficiency work.
faculty.key_paper_1: Visually Consistent Hierarchical Image Classification (HCAST), ICLR 2025

faculty.department: EECS — ECE Division; affiliated with MIDAS, MCAIM, MICDE
faculty.research_areas: Foundations of generative AI (diffusion and flow models); deep representation learning; low-dimensional structure in high-dimensional data; neural collapse; memorisation vs generalisation in generative models; ML for scientific applications; numerical optimisation
faculty.why_match: His ICLR'26 paper 'Generalization of Diffusion Models Arises with a Balanced Representation Space' is the theoretical statement of the empirical puzzle Akshat hit: a DDPM pretrained on unlabelled abdominal CT gave a frozen encoder that retained 86.9% of fine-tuned liver Dice but scored 0.654 on kidney — WORSE than a randomly initialised baseline at 0.899. Qu's claim is that whether a diffusion model generalises rather than memorises is governed by the balance of its learned representation space, which is precisely a testable explanation for why the prior transferred for one organ and collapsed for another. His earlier 'The Emergence of Reproducibility and Consistency in Diffusion Models' (ICML 2024, best paper at the NeurIPS'23 Diffusion Workshop) established that diffusion models converge to the same underlying low-dimensional structure across training runs — directly relevant to Akshat's methodological complaint about his own study, that it used a single seed and no SSL baselines, so 'diffusion specifically' was never isolated. Qu co-taught the ICASSP/ISIT 2026 tutorial 'Harnessing Low Dimensionality in Diffusion Models: From Theory to Practice' with Liyue Shen; a Qu–Shen pairing is the natural home for the theory-plus-medical-imaging version of Akshat's question.

faculty.department: EECS — Computer Science and Engineering; Michigan AI Lab core faculty
faculty.research_areas: Computer vision, graphics, generative modelling; 3D/4D reconstruction; diffusion models for scientific and medical problems; generative data augmentation; neural implicit representations (DeepSDF); uncertainty-aware multimodal sensor fusion
faculty.why_match: His preprint 'Generative Spatiotemporal Data Augmentation' (arXiv:2512.12508) is the same research move as Akshat's A-PDF: use a generative model to manufacture training data, then confront the question of whether the synthetic samples are actually usable. A-PDF trained a conditional WGAN-GP and then REFUSED to trust the discriminator, instead scoring generated masks against the class-proportion distribution of 447 real masks via Mahalanobis and kNN — retaining only 33.7% and 35.1% of 5,000 samples respectively, versus 86% for a naive per-class range filter. That is an explicit synthetic-data quality-control criterion, which is the open problem in generative augmentation. He is also the CSE-side anchor for medical generative imaging: 'Prospective Dynamic 3D MRI Reconstruction via Latent-Space Motion Tracking from Single Measurement' (CVPR 2026, with Liyue Shen) and 'Single-Spoke Motion-Compensated Dynamic 3D MRI Reconstruction via Neural Representation' (MICCAI 2025) — meaning an application naming Park reaches the Shen collaboration from inside CSE. Secondary hook: 'Cocoon: Robust Multi-Modal Perception With Uncertainty-Aware Sensor Fusion' (ICLR 2025) maps onto Akshat's LiDAR-camera fusion work as Perception Lead on the autonomous go-kart.
faculty.key_paper_2: Prospective Dynamic 3D MRI Reconstruction via Latent-Space Motion Tracking from Single Measurement, CVPR 2026 (with Liyue Shen)

faculty.why_match: Her group's 'Disparate Censorship & Undertesting: A Source of Label Bias in Clinical Machine Learning' (MLHC 2022) and 'Deep Learning Applied to Chest X-Rays: Exploiting and Preventing Shortcuts' (MLHC 2020) are data-centric arguments that a medical model's ceiling is set by label quality, not architecture — the same claim Akshat's polyp study makes quantitatively: holding the architecture FIXED and varying only preprocessing moved Dice by +0.0453 (U-Net), +0.0579 (ResU-Net) and +0.0226 (Attention U-Net), and the gain shrank as the backbone strengthened. Her recent 'Measuring Model Performance in the Presence of an Intervention' (AAAI 2026) and 'Cross-Validation for Longitudinal Datasets with Unstable Correlations' (KDD 2025) are evaluation-methodology papers of the type Akshat gravitates to as a self-described rigorous empiricist.

faculty.department: EECS — ECE Division; Professor (courtesy), Statistics; affiliated with MIDAS, Michigan AI Lab, CCMB
faculty.research_areas: Machine learning theory; classification with label noise; mixture proportion estimation; learning from label proportions; weakly supervised and semi-supervised learning; domain adaptation and generalisation; novelty detection; recently diffusion/flow methods (functional rectified flow, PU-guided diffusion sampling)
faculty.why_match: 'Label Noise: Ignorance is Bliss' (NeurIPS 2024, Zhu, Zhang, Gangrade, Scott) is the theoretical counterpart to Akshat's most quietly interesting empirical finding. In the lumbar-spine pseudo-labelling study the teacher (0.735 mIoU on 54 labelled images) produced noisy pseudo-labels, and Akshat tested filtering strategies head to head: per-class optimal thresholding raised pseudo-label IoU from 0.744 to 0.853 and the student to 0.816 mIoU (+8.1 points), MC-dropout uncertainty was merely comparable (0.791–0.792), and COMBINING the two added nothing. Scott's line of work asks exactly when it is provably better to ignore label noise than to correct for it — which is the formal version of 'the extra uncertainty machinery bought nothing'. His long programme on mixture proportion estimation ('Mixture Proportion Estimation Beyond Irreducibility', ICML 2023) is also the right formalism for A-PDF's class-proportion filter, which scores generated masks against the proportion distribution of real masks.
faculty.key_paper_1: Label Noise: Ignorance is Bliss, NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2411.00079)
faculty.key_paper_2: Mixture Proportion Estimation Beyond Irreducibility, ICML 2023

faculty.department: EECS — Computer Science and Engineering; Michigan AI Lab core faculty
faculty.research_areas: Machine learning and causal inference; data-efficient causal inference in resource-constrained settings; robust predictive models built from causal ideas; healthcare applications
faculty.why_match: Her stated programme is, verbatim, 'building data-efficient causal inference methods in resource-constrained settings, and building robust predictive ML models using ideas from causality' — the causal-inference sibling of Akshat's label-efficiency work, where a teacher trained on 54 labelled lumbar-spine images plus filtered pseudo-labels reached 0.816 mIoU and, more usefully, where per-class confidence thresholds calibrated on just 5 reference images matched those derived from 304.
